title: Hermite coefficients of a difference
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ both be square-integrable with respect to the $n$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure. For every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite coefficient of $f-g$ at $\alpha$ is the Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$ minus that of $g$ at $\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is in $L^2$ for the product standard Gaussian measure
$g$ is in $L^2$ for the product standard Gaussian measure
